verses.text: Peter and John were going up to the temple for prayer at the ninth hour.
A man who had been unable to walk since birth was being carried in. Every day, people set him by the temple gate called Beautiful so he could ask those entering for help.
When he saw Peter and John about to enter the temple, he asked them for help too.
Peter looked straight at him, and John did too. Peter said, “Look at us.”
The man focused on them, expecting to get something.
Peter said, “I don’t have silver or gold. But I’ll give you what I do have: in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, get up and walk!”
Peter took him by the right hand and helped him up. At once his feet and ankles became strong.
He jumped up, stood, and started walking. Then he went into the temple with them, walking, leaping, and praising God. 🙌
Everyone saw him walking and praising God.
They recognized him as the man who used to sit and beg for help at the temple’s Beautiful Gate. They were completely amazed at what had happened to him.
The man who had been healed held on to Peter and John. Everyone came running to them at the porch called Solomon’s, stunned by what they saw.
Peter saw the crowd and said, “People of Israel, why are you amazed at this? Why are you staring at us as if our own power or goodness made this man walk?
The God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—the God of our ancestors—has honored his servant Jesus. You handed Jesus over and rejected him in front of Pilate, even though Pilate had decided to release him.
You rejected the Holy and Righteous One and asked Pilate to release a murderer instead.
You killed the Prince of life, but God raised him from the dead. We saw it ourselves.
Faith in Jesus’ name has made this man strong. You see him here and know who he is. Faith in Jesus has made him completely well, right in front of all of you.
“Now, brothers and sisters, I know you and your leaders acted in ignorance.
But this is how God fulfilled what he had announced through all the prophets: that his Messiah would suffer.
So turn back to God and return to him, so your sins can be wiped away. Then times of refreshing can come from the Lord’s presence,
and he can send Jesus the Messiah appointed for you.
Heaven must receive Jesus until the time comes for everything to be restored, just as God said long ago through his holy prophets.
Moses said to our ancestors, ‘The Lord your God will raise up a prophet for you from among your own people, like me. Listen to everything he tells you.
Anyone who refuses to listen to that prophet will be completely removed from the people.’
All the prophets who spoke—from Samuel onward—also announced these days.
You are the descendants of the prophets and heirs of the covenant God made with your ancestors when he told Abraham, ‘Through your descendant, all the families of the earth will be blessed.’
When God raised up his servant Jesus, he sent him first to you to bless you by turning every one of you away from your evil ways.”
